summary: The 24-cell: 24 corners at every arrangement of (±1, ±1, 0, 0), 96 equal edges; its three inscribed 16-cells in three colors.

claims.claim: 24 corners at the arrangements of (±1, ±1, 0, 0), 96 edges and 24 octahedral cells; the corners split into three 16-cells.
claims.how: polytope() builds the corners from their coordinates and joins every pair at the shortest distance; a test checks the counts, the degrees and that every edge has the same length.

sources.title: 24-cell
sources.says: Its vertices are the 24 coordinate permutations of (±1, ±1, 0, 0); 24 vertices, 96 edges, 24 octahedral cells; it contains three 8-point 16-cells.

claims.test: tests/mt2.spec.mjs: the 4D shapes have the right corners, edges and degrees, all edges equal

claims.claim: It turns in four dimensions and is shown in perspective from a point out along the fourth axis.
claims.how: Each frame the corners are turned in the planes of x and w and of y and w, then projected by xyz × 2.4 / (2.4 − w); the edges are straight lines between the projected corners.

sources.title: Tesseract (projections)
sources.says: A 4D shape can be shown in 3D by perspective projection from a point outside it in the fourth dimension.

claims.test: tests/mt2.spec.mjs: the 4D shapes roll a whole turn and end where they rest

simplified: Only the corners and edges are drawn; the faces and cells are left out so the inside can be seen.
The view is a 3D shadow of the 4D shape, so edges can look different lengths and can cross.
